items.title: Ralph Humphrey interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003
items.q: he called me up and said do you want to come down and audition for the band... I went ahead and went down for the audition... playing with the band

ctx.x: And how did you handle that stuff that was in this outlandish —

Well it’s a curious thing. I guess — well I had been turned on to Don’s music maybe two or three months before I had the chance to meet him. Because our stage band director at San Jose State said guys check this out, so he brought in I think “Live at Monterey” which was Don’s first record. And we sat there and we listened to it and all of our jaws dropped because we just never heard anything like it, ever, anywhere. And all I knew up to that point was a little bit of Dave Brubeck and that was it for as far as odd…

because of the instructor. And he was kind of a zany guy anyhow so he liked all the new stuff. He’d sometimes have us rehearse with all the lights off, and say okay let’s just play anything you want to play. So we were experimenting. So when Don came along it was perfect. And for me I was just trying to feel my way through it and read the charts. I didn’t know where it was coming from or any of the concepts of the rhythms. That came later. That actually came after I joined the band. But the ability to pick up on…
